kind: pre-product-fix diagnostic plan, not an oracle result or acceptance gate
purpose: Observe a quiet target while unrelated changes exceed retained history, then resume and mutate it; investigate r48 terminal cache-watcher behavior.
serverLifecycle: Externally managed, sequential official Java then current Fireside, on a quiescent host; never launch, stop, or signal a server from this capture.
transport: gRPC Listen; decoded response messages, not raw HTTP/2 or WebChannel byte frames
workload: Create an exclusively owned random namespace and one quiet synthetic target document.
Open one raw query Listen and one 7.11.6 query onSnapshot for that target collection; require their initial observation and an observed raw resume token before proceeding.

For churn cases, create 4100 unrelated tiny documents in 4100 acknowledged sequential single-document commits within 180 seconds; neither watched collection nor target document changes. The idle control performs none.
Leave both listeners open for 150 seconds after the writes (or after initial readiness in the idle control); observe all frames and callbacks without predicting any heartbeat cadence.

Only in churn-forced, cancel the owned low-level client stream and open another raw Listen using the latest token actually observed on the first stream. Natural/control cases do not deliberately disconnect either listener.

For forced reattachment observe at most 30 seconds, preserving rejection or silence; do not invent a fallback token or silently reopen without it. Instrument the high-level SDK's actual Listen calls separately to observe natural reconnection without forcing it.
Change the target version from 0 to 1 and observe the active raw stream and high-level delivery for at most 30 seconds, even if forced reattachment was rejected.
Close owned client streams, delete only documents within the acknowledged exclusively owned namespace under a 120-second cleanup budget, and retain all failure evidence.
interpretation: Capture completion is not a compatibility pass. Report actual stream, token, callback, mutation-delivery and cleanup outcomes for both oracles before proposing a product change. External launcher must record exact binary/jar identity and host preflight separately.
